reason: The passage portrays the Hebrews (עִבְרִיֹּת/עִבְרִיּוֹת) as a distinct collective people rather than merely a family or religious community. Key indicators include: (1) the use of 'עָם' (people/nation) in reference to them as a growing demographic entity ('וַיִּרֶב הָעָם'); (2) institutional organization through midwives serving them as a community; (3) their portrayal as a distinct ethnic group requiring specific laws from Pharaoh, implying political and demographic significance; (4) the consistent delineation of 'Hebrew women' and 'Hebrew children' as a identifiable national/ethnic category separate from Egyptians. While the text includes a religious dimension (fear of God), the primary framing emphasizes them as a socio-political entity of sufficient size and organization to concern the Egyptian ruler, rather than focusing on their religious identity as followers of Yahweh.
